name: The Yogācāra entry through mind-only to the grounds (Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 14)

stages.name: saṃbhāra
stages.description: Accumulating merit and knowledge; hearing and reflecting on the teachings; calm and insight joined.

stages.name: uṣmagata
stages.description: In concentration, objects are no longer seen apart from mental speech.

stages.name: mūrdhan
stages.description: Firm vigour increases the light of the Dharma.

stages.name: kṣānti
stages.description: Abiding in mind-only, all objects seen as appearances of mind; the distraction of the grasped is abandoned.

stages.name: laukikāgradharma
stages.description: Only the distraction of the grasper remains; the immediate concentration is touched.

stages.name: darśana-mārga / prathamā bhūmi
stages.description: Supramundane non-conceptual wisdom free of duality; the first transformation of the basis.

stages.name: bhāvanā-mārga
stages.description: The two knowledges cultivated through the remaining grounds over two incalculable aeons.

stages.name: vajropama-samādhi / niṣṭhāśrayaparāvṛtti
stages.description: Final transformation of the basis, free of all obscurations; omniscience.

stages.name: sattvārtha
stages.description: Established there, the buddha works for the welfare of all beings through the three bodies and four wisdoms.

notes: Bands assigned by U41 (interpretation layer); logged.

name: The five stages of cognition-only practice (Cheng weishi lun)

stages.name: ziliang wei 資糧位
stages.description: Gathering merit and wisdom; faith in and understanding of cognition-only, but the latent twofold grasping not yet subdued.

stages.name: jiaxing wei 加行位
stages.description: The four aids to penetration: the grasped and then the grasper are seen as empty.

stages.name: tongda wei 通達位
stages.description: Non-conceptual wisdom realizes suchness: the path of seeing.

stages.name: xiuxi wei 修習位
stages.description: Repeated cultivation through the ten grounds, abandoning the seeds of the two obscurations.

stages.name: jiujing wei 究竟位
stages.description: Buddhahood: the transformation of the basis, the four wisdoms and the three bodies.

name: The seven attentions to the first absorption (Śrāvakabhūmi)

stages.name: lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī manaskāra
stages.description: Discerning the coarseness of sense-pleasures and the peace of the first absorption.

stages.name: ādhimokṣika
stages.description: Resolving on that understanding beyond hearing and reflection.

stages.name: prāvivekya
stages.description: Abandoning the strongest afflictions of the desire realm.

stages.name: ratisaṃgrāhaka
stages.description: Delighting in the abandonment and abandoning the middling afflictions.

stages.name: mīmāṃsā
stages.description: Examining whether desire remains.

stages.name: prayoganiṣṭha
stages.description: Abandoning the subtle afflictions; the preparatory stage completed.

stages.name: prayoganiṣṭhāphala
stages.description: Entering the first absorption proper.

notes: Names checked in the e-text; the functions of stages 2–6 are recalled from the standard explanation.

name: The twelve bodhisattva abodes and the Tathāgata's abode (Bodhisattvabhūmi)

stages.name: gotra-vihāra
stages.description: The bodhisattva with the lineage before arousing the resolve.

stages.name: adhimukticaryā-vihāra
stages.description: From the arising of the resolve up to the pure intention.

stages.name: pramudita-vihāra
stages.description: The pure intention; first ground.

stages.name: adhiśīla-vihāra
stages.description: Second ground.

stages.name: adhicitta-vihāra
stages.description: Third ground.

stages.name: adhiprajña-vihāra: bodhipakṣya
stages.description: Fourth ground.

stages.name: adhiprajña-vihāra: satya
stages.description: Fifth ground.

stages.name: adhiprajña-vihāra: pratītyasamutpāda
stages.description: Sixth ground.

stages.name: sābhisaṃskāra nirnimitta vihāra
stages.description: Seventh ground.

stages.name: anābhoga nirnimitta vihāra
stages.description: Eighth ground.

stages.name: pratisaṃvid-vihāra
stages.description: Ninth ground.

stages.name: parama vihāra
stages.description: Tenth ground.

stages.name: tāthāgata vihāra
stages.description: Unsurpassed abode of awakening.

notes: Names checked in the e-text; the correlation of abodes 3–12 with grounds 1–10 follows the text's own later bhūmi-paṭala as recalled.
